intro: The vocabulary of history books: reigns, wars, treaties and the centuries, with a short look at Spain's own past.
b1.texto:
**Time.** **El siglo** is written in Roman numerals and read as a cardinal number: **el siglo XV** is el siglo quince. **A principios de**, **a mediados de**, **a finales de** siglo. **La época**, **la era**, **la Edad Media**, **la Edad Moderna**. **Antes de Cristo** (a. C.) and **después de Cristo** (d. C.).

**Power.** **Un rey** has **un reinado**; **un emperador**, **un imperio**. **Gobernar**, **reinar**, **heredar el trono**, **abdicar**.

**War.** **Estalla** una guerra. **El ejército** **invade** un país, **lucha en** una batalla, **vence a** su enemigo or sufre **una derrota**. The loser **se rinde**. Countries on the same side are **aliados**. At the end, they **firman un tratado de paz**.

**The tenses of history.** The indefinido tells the events: **estalló**, **duró**, **murió**. The imperfect describes the background: **era**, **había**, **vivían**. The historical present makes them vivid: en 1492 Colón **llega** a América. And the passive is common: **fue conquistada**, **fue firmado**.

**Spain in one paragraph.** The Romans called it Hispania. From 711 much of the peninsula was Muslim **al-Ándalus**, for almost eight centuries. In 1492 the Catholic Monarchs took Granada and Columbus reached America. **La Guerra Civil** lasted from 1936 to 1939 and was followed by **la dictadura** of Franco, who died in 1975. Then came **la Transición** to democracy and the Constitution of 1978.
b2.f0: The Spanish Civil War broke out in July 1936, when part of the army rebelled against the government of the Republic.
b2.f1: What some rebels expected to resolve in a few days lasted almost three years and divided entire families.
b2.f2: Both sides received foreign support, and the conflict is also studied in relation to the tensions that led to the Second World War.
b2.f3: The Republic was defeated in April 1939; hundreds of thousands of people crossed the border into exile.
b2.f4: A dictatorship followed and ended with Franco dying in 1975.
b2.f5: During the transition, amnesty measures were passed and political reconciliation was prioritised, but their effects and limits remain debated.
b2.f6: Almost a century later, the war remains present in politics, literature and the memory of many families.
